lines.trans: Just an ordinary broom.
As if he were still right here with us.
Dmitriy Vladimirovich.
I am afraid things will not work the way they used to.
Today guests have already canceled their banquet.
Because Viktor Petrovich will not be doing the cooking.
We all pitch in and work at full capacity.
Where were you?
We were mopping the floors.
Nastya and I did that too.
Ironing the laundry.
Nastya came up with that idea.
Why did I even tell you about that.

meanings.note: a large formal meal for many people

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.
A lavish banquet was hosted in the restaurant.

meanings.note: Постельное бельё = bed linen. Common neuter noun meaning 'linen, laundry; underwear' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'linen, laundry; underwear' in everyday Russian.
Нижнее бельё. Common neuter noun meaning 'linen, laundry; underwear' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У него даже постельного белья нет.
examples.trans: He doesn't even have bed linen.
Clean linen is in the wardrobe.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, вы со всей квартиры бельё принесли! У меня уже спина болит.
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you brought laundry from the whole flat! My back is hurting already.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'бояться собак'. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be afraid (of), to fear'.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Usually как будто. Core Russian conj meaning 'as if, as though' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.en: short-handled household broom (traditionally made of twigs or sorghum)
meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'besom, short broom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Tie a broom to a mop!
Take the broom and sweep the kitchen.

examples.text: Когда нет в кармане денег. Привяжи ты к швабре веник!
examples.trans: When there is no money in your pocket. Tie a broom to a mop!

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Clean with water. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wash', paired with 'помыть'.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

examples.text: Пока ещё на мои деньги куплен! Встала и мыть посуду, шагом марш!
examples.trans: It's still bought with my money! Get up and wash the dishes, forward march!

meanings.note: Colloquial with на. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'валиваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pile on, dig in', paired with 'навалиться'.

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pile on, dig in', paired with 'навалиться'.

examples.trans: To lean on with all one's weight.

examples.text: Давай скорее наваливайся на эту вкусную икру.
examples.trans: Come on quickly help yourself to this tasty caviar.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'return, dedication, pass' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наваливаемся и работаем с полной отдачей.
examples.trans: We all pitch in and work at full capacity.
Will you give her to me?

meanings.note: intransitive reflexive verb with infinitive or от + genitive

examples.trans: He refused to sign the report.
Really? Did he refuse to sign it?

meanings.en: still, as before, just as previously
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-прежнему').

examples.text: От вас я по-прежнему жду участия.
examples.trans: I still expect participation from you.

examples.text: Они по-прежнему живут в этом доме.
examples.trans: They still live in this building.

examples.text: От вас я по-прежнему жду участия. Всё.
examples.trans: I still expect participation from you. That is all.

погладить.gloss: to stroke, to caress, to pet

meanings.en: to stroke, to pet, to caress
meanings.note: Pass hand gently over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'гладить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stroke, to caress, to pet', paired with 'гладить'.

examples.trans: Just stroke the hand more gently.
The girl gently stroked the white cat.

meanings.note: На полу = on the floor. Common masculine noun meaning 'floor' in everyday Russian.

Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: adverb or conjunction in 'прежде чем'

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: Простые люди = ordinary people. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple; ordinary').

Простые люди = ordinary people. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple; ordinary').

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.
